page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-160GB-2xRTXPRO6000 is an accelerator-focused instance engineered for compute-heavy parallel workloads. The server combines 32 x86_64 cores from an AMD EPYC 9555 processor operating at 2.0 GHz with 160 GB of system memory, yielding 5 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs based on the Blackwell architecture, providing an aggregate of 192 GB of total VRAM. The host does not include local disk storage, necessitating attached network volumes for persistent storage, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier computational performance across several vector and memory benchmarks. The AMD EPYC host processor achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 2678.0 and a multi-core score of 24400.0, supported by instruction set capabilities including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16). Memory throughput is a prominent strength, measuring 455.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 228.66 GB/sec for writes. In language model evaluations, the dual-GPU configuration achieves top-tier inference throughput, processing prompts at 8118.49 tokens per second and generating text at 221.74 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The instance delivers high resource density for parallel tasks, pairing substantial GPU memory capacity with robust host CPU throughput. Because local storage is absent and CPU allocation uses shared scheduling, performance consistency relies on architectural alignment with network-attached storage throughput. The platform is structured for large-scale AI model inference, GPU-accelerated ray tracing, image generation pipelines, and complex scientific simulation workflows.
description: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-160GB-2xRTXPRO6000 is a GPU-accelerated server tailored for deep learning inference, 3D rendering, and parallel computing. It features 32 x86_64 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9555 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, alongside 160 GB of RAM. The compute payload is driven by dual NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs delivering 192 GB of combined VRAM. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. In benchmark testing, the system exhibits top-tier uncached memory read bandwidth of 455.64 GB/sec and strong multi-core computational throughput, processing 7B model prompts at 8118.49 tokens per second. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network volumes. The instance provides a high-density accelerator footprint fit for multi-GPU inference, rendering engines, and scientific processing tasks.
